interface_note: Only parameter values vary; all mathematical conditions and requested quantity remain those stated by the supplied source questions. Names describe source data, not a target algorithm. Implement solve(parameters), no natural-language applicability detection. max_length must not exceed the number of distinct supplied digits.

analysis.invalid_operation: Manual or partially manual enumeration of permutations with hand primality checks, especially for the 4-digit case, followed by truncation or guessing/recalling the count for the largest length instead of computing it.
observations: All source tasks share one deterministic counting problem: given a digit set and max_length, count distinct primes obtainable by arranging 1..max_length distinct digits without repetition, with no leading zero.

The failing trajectories consistently attempt manual enumeration and primality testing, then truncate or guess the 4-digit count; several final answers are explicitly guessed or recalled rather than computed.
The attempted solutions rely on hand-checking divisibility and on unverified counts for the largest length, which is the main source of wrong totals.
A trustworthy procedure exists: exhaustive enumeration of all valid digit permutations up to max_length, deduplication, and exact primality testing by trial division up to the integer square root.
The search space is tiny (at most sum over k<=4 of P(n,k) <= 10*9*8*7 + ... < 6000 candidates), so exhaustive enumeration is feasible and exact.
analysis.procedure_plan: Implement solve(parameters) with digits and max_length. Normalize digits to a sorted unique list. For each length k from 1 to min(max_length, len(digits)), generate all ordered k-tuples of distinct digits from the set (permutations without repetition). For each tuple, reject if the first digit is 0 (leading zero). Form the integer value. Insert into a set to deduplicate (though distinct tuples with distinct digits already give distinct integers, dedup is harmless). For each candidate integer n, test primality exactly: if n < 2 reject; if n in {2,3} accept; if n even or divisible by 3 reject; otherwise trial-divide by all integers d from 5 while d*d <= n, stepping d by 2 and 6 alternately (or simply all odd d), rejecting on any exact divisor; accept if none found. Count accepted candidates. Return the count. Use integer arithmetic only; no floating point. Ensure max_length is clamped to the number of distinct digits.
analysis.replacement_operation: Exhaustive programmatic enumeration of all valid digit permutations for each length up to max_length, with exact deterministic primality testing by trial division up to the integer square root, and counting the accepted distinct primes.
analysis.uncertainty: Low uncertainty about the enumeration and primality procedure; it is exact and the search space is small. The only residual risk is implementation detail (leading-zero handling and deduplication), which is straightforward. The diagnosis that manual enumeration/guessing caused the failures is strongly supported by the truncated and guessed final answers, but the exact internal arithmetic error in each attempt is not individually established.
